title: "To God Be Glory! Peace on Earth!"
description: "To God Be Glory! Peace on Earth!" in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 422, “Glory to God, Through Peace on Earth”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: "To God be glo-ry! Peace on earth!" Let us re-peat a-gain The hymn that hailed the Sav-iour's birth, "Peace and good will to men!"

lines: "To God be glory! Peace on earth!"
The hymn that hailed the Saviour's birth, —
Good will to men! O God, we hail
This of Thy law the sum;
For as this shall o'er earth prevail,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
